\newcommand{\ReplayAbstract}{On a real cluster it resizes pods in place without restarts, and a small trace replay against the HPA (3 seeds) shows CHIMERA on or below the HPA's cost--violation frontier: 7 of 9 HPA runs were dominated by a CHIMERA run with the same seed, and no CHIMERA run was dominated.}
\newcommand{\ReplayBody}{An open-loop load generator replayed a 24-minute demand trace (12 minutes of an Azure trace, then a flash crowd to five times the mean) against a CPU-bound service costing 61\,ms of CPU per request, with a 0.3\,s latency objective (five times the service time, as in the simulator). Each controller started from the same allocation with three unscored lead-in minutes, and both sides could reach the same ten cores. We ran the HPA at three utilisation targets and CHIMERA at 3 settings, so that each has a cost frontier, with 3 seeds each (Table~\ref{tab:replay}, Fig.~\ref{fig:replay}). CHIMERA used a request-rate signal; no run restarted a container.

\begin{table}[t]
\caption{Live replay, mean of 3 seeds. Viol.\ = requests over 0.3\,s (\%), with the range over seeds; $>$1\,s = requests over one second (\%); CPU in core-minutes.}
\label{tab:replay}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrrr@{}}
\toprule
Controller & Viol. & Range & $>$1\,s & CPU \\
\midrule
HPA, 70\,\% target & 48.9 & 44.1--55.2 & 39.3 & 85.3 \\
HPA, 50\,\% target & 23.5 & 21.9--26.4 & 14.9 & 102.4 \\
HPA, 35\,\% target & 16.3 & 11.2--22.5 & 5.4 & 124.3 \\
\midrule
CHIMERA, 0.46 (default) & 32.1 & 26.2--43.1 & 20.9 & 80.9 \\
CHIMERA, 0.35 & 14.6 & 12.1--18.7 & 7.1 & 93.6 \\
CHIMERA, 0.25 & 7.0 & 6.6--7.7 & 3.2 & 108.1 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

Of the 9 HPA runs, 7 were dominated by a CHIMERA run with the same seed: one that used no more CPU and missed the objective less often. Of the 9 CHIMERA runs, 0 were dominated by an HPA run. For the 6 CHIMERA runs whose cost lay inside the range spanned by the HPA settings, interpolating the HPA's violation rate at the same cost gave CHIMERA fewer violations in 5, with a mean gap of +11.9 points. At setting 0.35 CHIMERA averaged 14.6\,\% violations for 93.6 core-minutes, against 16.3\,\% for 124.3 with the HPA at its most generous setting. One CHIMERA run (seed 2, setting 0.25) was repeated. In the first attempt the service was slow whatever it was given (median latency 0.31\,s with four to ten cores allocated for at most three cores of demand, and 20540 requests issued where the other runs issued about 22\,600), which points to interference on the host and not to a control decision; it had 50.9\,\% violations. Counting that attempt instead of the repeat, 7 of 9 HPA runs are dominated and 1 of 9 CHIMERA runs. Both attempts are in the repository. With 3 seeds, one service and one trace this is indicative, not a significance result, and the spread between seeds is large. Every controller missed the objective far more often than in simulation: a 61\,ms request on a pod limited to half a core exceeds a single CFS quota period, so the simulator's latency law is kinder than this service.}
\newcommand{\ReplayConclusion}{On a real cluster a small trace-replay experiment shows CHIMERA on or below the HPA's cost--violation frontier: 7 of 9 HPA runs were dominated by a CHIMERA run with the same seed, and no CHIMERA run was dominated. A larger live study, with more seeds, more services and a simulator whose latency law is fitted to measurements, is the main work that remains.}
